name: Waseda (Tokyo Sakura Tram (Toden Arakawa Line))
tagline: Shinjuku in 28 minutes and Shibuya in 29 minutes. Served by 1 line.
summary: The station is in Shinjuku City, where the Tokyo Metropolitan Bureau of Transportation run 1 line between them. Journey times to the main business districts are 37 minutes to Otemachi, 28 minutes to Shinjuku, 29 minutes to Shibuya and 54 minutes to Shinagawa. The station stands 7.7 m above sea level, and the ground within 800 m varies in height by 19.0 m. The land around the station has gentle slopes.

terrain.note: The station sits lower than the ground around it, at 7.7 m above sea level. Within 800 m the ground ranges from 7.5 m to 26.5 m, a difference of 19.0 m.

hazards: On the flood hazard map for the largest rainfall the government models, the station itself falls inside the projected inundation area, to a projected depth of 0.5 to 3 m. Of the nine points within 400 m of the station, 5 also fall inside the area, and the deepest projection is 3 to 5 m. On the whole, the flood projection here is on the small side for the 23 wards.

medical: Within an 800 m walk of the station there are 7 clinics and 11 pharmacies. Day-to-day care is available close to the station. The nearest hospital is 大同病院, about 15 minutes' walk from the station. The next nearest is 国立国際医療センター, about 17 minutes' walk. "Hospital" here means a facility OpenStreetMap records as one. OpenStreetMap does not record whether a facility admits inpatients or which departments it runs, so check each one on its own website. For which clinics open at night and at weekends, ask the emergency advice line of the ward you live in.

congestion: The ministry's congestion survey does not publish figures for Tokyo Sakura Tram (Toden Arakawa Line). It covers the major commuter stretches, and this line is not among them.

neighbours.lead: Omokagebashi is ahead on how little of the area is in the flood projection, but Waseda (Tokyo Sakura Tram (Toden Arakawa Line)) is ahead on how easy the shopping is.
